whats your take on the code review Code Review — PR #817: Reversible deletes + media trash/retention (#760)                                                                                                                                 │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ Scope reviewed: full diff (15 files, +655), plus surrounding base code                                                                                                                                   │
   │ (storage.py, activity.py, deletion_sweeper.py, storage_usage.py,                                                                                                                                         │
   │ activity_query.py, delete routes for members/gallery/documents, frontend                                                                                                                                 │
   │ ActivityView). Branch feat/760-reversible-deletes-media-retention is checked                                                                                                                             │
   │ out locally; verified uv run pytest tests/test_activity.py tests/test_storage.py                                                                                                                         │
   │ → all pass.                                                                                                                                                                                              │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ Verdict: Solid, well-scoped PR. Follows the #572 pattern faithfully,                                                                                                                                     │
   │ transactional ordering is correct, security posture is preserved, tests/docs/                                                                                                                            │
   │ changelog/i18n are all in order. No blockers. Findings are low-severity                                                                                                                                  │
   │ robustness items plus design points worth challenging.                                                                                                                                                   │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ What's done well                                                                                                                                                                                         │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ • Snapshot-before-delete / trash-after-commit ordering is right everywhere —                                                                                                                             │
   │   a failed commit can't strand a live row pointing at moved bytes.                                                                                                                                       │
   │ • The previously unlogged DELETE /documents/{id}/files/{file_id} endpoint was                                                                                                                            │
   │   a real audit gap; the fix also adds the missing activity.entry_added                                                                                                                                   │
   │   publish.                                                                                                                                                                                               │
   │ • trash_media reuses _safe_media_path / _safe_original_files, so the                                                                                                                                     │
   │   existing traversal protections carry over. Verified the .trash collision                                                                                                                               │
   │   claim: _SAFE_PATH_SEGMENT_RE (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$) does forbid a                                                                                                                              │
   │   leading dot, so no tree dir can be named .trash.                                                                                                                                                       │
   │ • Purge runs under the existing advisory-lock leader election                                                                                                                                            │
   │   (_sweep_if_leader → _run_sweep_once), safe for multi-worker.                                                                                                                                           │
   │ • New document_file target type checked against the restricted-membership                                                                                                                                │
   │   hiding map (ACTIVITY_TARGET_TYPES_BY_DOMAIN): only tasks is restrictable                                                                                                                               │
   │   today, so no activity-log info leak. Frontend renders details only for                                                                                                                                 │
   │   update actions, so the big snapshot JSON never hits the UI.                                                                                                                                            │
   │ • Golden rules respected: no version bump, changelog under ## [Unreleased],                                                                                                                              │
   │   i18n parity (only en/de locales exist), Alembic correctly not needed.                                                                                                                                  │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ Findings (by severity)                                                                                                                                                                                   │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 1. Low — mtime race defeats retention for old files (storage.py,                                                                                                                                         │
   │    trash_media). shutil.move preserves the original mtime;                                                                                                                                               │
   │    os.utime(dest, None) stamps the move time only afterwards. A file uploaded                                                                                                                            │
   │    │ 30 days ago has an already-expired mtime in the window between move and                                                                                                                             │
   │    │ utime — a concurrent sweep purges it instantly. Worse: if os.utime fails,                                                                                                                           │
   │    │ the exception is swallowed and the file is purged at the next sweep,                                                                                                                                │
   │    │ silently voiding the 30-day retention. Stamping the source before the                                                                                                                               │
   │    │ move (or encoding the trash timestamp in the dest name) closes this.                                                                                                                                │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 2. Low — silent failure mode is worse than delete_media's (storage.py).                                                                                                                                  │
   │    trash_media swallows all OSError/ValueError with no logging. A failed                                                                                                                                 │
   │    move leaves the bytes in the live tree dir with the DB row already gone:                                                                                                                              │
   │    the file counts against quota forever and is never purged (it's not in                                                                                                                                │
   │    .trash). delete_media had the same never-raise contract, so this is                                                                                                                                   │
   │    parity not regression — but trash now carries the retention promise, so at                                                                                                                            │
   │    minimum a logger.warning is warranted.                                                                                                                                                                │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 3. Low — mtime as the retention clock is fragile. Any external touch                                                                                                                                     │
   │    (rsync, backup restore, admin poking around) shifts mtimes and extends or                                                                                                                             │
   │    shortens retention unpredictably. A timestamped filename prefix or a small                                                                                                                            │
   │    manifest would be robust; the current design is schema-free and simple,                                                                                                                               │
   │    which is a fair trade while no restore endpoint exists — but it should be a                                                                                                                           │
   │    conscious decision.                                                                                                                                                                                   │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 4. Nit — purge leaves empty dirs forever (purge_expired_media_trash).                                                                                                                                    │
   │    Files are unlinked but .trash/ and .trash/originals/ are never removed;                                                                                                                               │
   │    one empty pair per tree-with-deletions accumulates. Also, trash_media on                                                                                                                              │
   │    a missing file can still create empty .trash dirs via                                                                                                                                                 │
   │    _trash_originals_dir.                                                                                                                                                                                 │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 5. Nit — no test for the quota exclusion. _media_bytes skipping .trash                                                                                                                                   │
   │    is the user-visible "deleting frees quota immediately" promise, but no test                                                                                                                           │
   │    covers it. Also untested: trash_media with only an originals/ sibling                                                                                                                                 │
   │    present (display file missing).                                                                                                                                                                       │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 6. Nit — cosmetic inconsistencies: delete_document trashes before                                                                                                                                        │
   │    publishing events, delete_image trashes after (harmless);                                                                                                                                             │
   │    purge_expired_media_trash(MEDIA_TRASH_TTL_SECONDS) passes the default                                                                                                                                 │
   │    explicitly; the document_file snapshot is built inline in the route while                                                                                                                             │
   │    the other four types get service-level helpers (a                                                                                                                                                     │
   │    document_file_delete_snapshot() would be symmetric — the docs justify the                                                                                                                             │
   │    inline form, so take or leave).                                                                                                                                                                       │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ 7. Non-issue, checked: trash filename collisions (shutil.move overwrites                                                                                                                                 │
   │    an existing dest on POSIX) are practically impossible with UUID filenames.                                                                                                                            │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ Challenges to the implementation                                                                                                                                                                         │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ • Quota freed instantly, disk held 30 days. Net disk usage can now grow by                                                                                                                               │
   │   up to 30 days of deletes, invisible to the quota system. On disk-constrained                                                                                                                           │
   │   self-hosts the fixed MEDIA_TRASH_TTL_SECONDS can't be tuned. The "no                                                                                                                                   │
   │   restore endpoint → internal detail" rationale is reasonable, but an env                                                                                                                                │
   │   override costs almost nothing. At minimum, ops docs should mention the new                                                                                                                             │
   │   disk-usage behaviour.                                                                                                                                                                                  │
   │ • Retention story is still incomplete for the undo goal. Member photos are                                                                                                                               │
   │   neither deleted nor trashed on delete_member (pre-existing: bytes become                                                                                                                               │
   │   permanent orphans that count against quota), and save_document's in-place                                                                                                                              │
   │   file removals remain immediate unlinks (acknowledged in the docs). Fine as                                                                                                                             │
   │   scoping, but the docs' "every delete action now carries a re-insertable                                                                                                                                │
   │   pre-image" is only true because member photos were never cleaned up at all —                                                                                                                           │
   │   worth flagging when undo is actually built.                                                                                                                                                            │
   │ • Backups grow silently. backup_service rglobs the entire media root, so                                                                                                                                 │
   │   archives now include up to 30 days of trashed bytes. Arguably desirable                                                                                                                                │
   │   (trash survives in backups), but it should be a deliberate choice, not a                                                                                                                               │
   │   side effect.                                                                                                                                                                                           │
   │ • Snapshot ↔ trash-path coupling. The snapshot stores the original media                                                                                                                                 │
   │   URL, not the trash location; a future undo must recompute                                                                                                                                              │
   │   .trash/<name> (and .trash/originals/) from trash_media's internals.                                                                                                                                    │
   │   Recording the trashed path (or documenting the on-disk contract as part of                                                                                                                             │
   │   snapshot version: 1) would decouple undo from those internals before the                                                                                                                               │
   │   payload shape ossifies.                                                                                                                                                                                │
   │ • Efficiency: no concerns. 2–3 extra indexed SELECTs per delete, one                                                                                                                                     │
   │   relative_to per file in the usage walk, purge scoped to .trash dirs                                                                                                                                    │
   │   only. All negligible.                                                                                                                                                                                  │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ Suggested outcome                                                                                                                                                                                        │
   │                                                                                                                                                                                                          │
   │ Approve as-is or with follow-ups: findings 1–2 (mtime race, silent-failure                                                                                                                               │
   │ logging) are the only ones I'd ask to be addressed — small, localized changes                                                                                                                            │
   │ in trash_media. The rest are follow-up material.

**Verified accurate:**

Finding 5 is a real gap, not a nitpick.

**My take on calibration:**

- **Findings 1 & 2 (mtime race, silent-failure logging) are the right things to flag but the review's own framing overstates finding 1.** The "race window" is two syscalls apart in a single synchronous call path — a concurrent sweep would need to land in a sub-millisecond gap on a file whose mtime is *already* 30 days stale. That's astronomically unlikely as a *timing* race. The finding that actually matters is the second half: if `os.utime` throws (rare, but real on some filesystems/permission setups) the exception is swallowed by the outer `except`, and the file is left in trash with its **original** mtime — silently voiding retention with no log line to explain why a file vanished. That's worth a one-line fix (log on failure, maybe stat-check before assuming success), but I'd present it as a robustness/observability gap, not a race condition — calling it a "race" invites arguing about locks when the fix is just "log it."
- **Finding 5 (no quota-exclusion test) is legitimate and cheap to fix** — it's the user-visible guarantee of the whole feature ("deleting frees quota now"), and it's currently only exercised implicitly.
- **The "challenges" section is the most valuable part of the review**, not the numbered findings. Quota-freed-but-disk-held-30-days and the snapshot-not-recording-trash-path points are real design decisions being made by default rather than on purpose. I'd push harder on the snapshot/trash-path coupling than the review does: baking `.trash/<name>` as an implicit, undocumented derivation from `trash_media`'s internals is exactly the kind of thing that becomes a silent bug the day someone reorganizes trash layout for the eventual undo feature. Key correction to the brief: **storage.py has no existing logger.** There is no `import logging` and no `logger = ...` in the file (confirmed by grep). So the logging fix must also add the logger. The established convention across `app/services/` is split — some use `logging.getLogger(__name__)` (cache, presence, job_service) and some use an explicit dotted string (`"app.deletion_sweeper"`, `"app.backup_service"`). Since `trash_media` is invoked from the deletion-sweep path and its sibling `purge_expired_media_trash` docstring already references `app.services.deletion_sweeper`, either works; I recommend `logging.getLogger(__name__)` (resolves to `app.services.storage`) as the lightest idiomatic choice used by the majority of newer service modules.

`shutil.move` semantics confirmed against the reasoning in the brief:
- Same filesystem → `os.rename`, which does not alter mtime (source mtime carried through verbatim).
- Cross filesystem → `copy2` (copies mtime from source) + `unlink`.
- Either way, stamping the **source** mtime before the move survives the move. So the fix is to `os.utime(source, None)` before `shutil.move` and drop the post-move `os.utime(dest, None)`. Bonus: if `os.utime` raises, it now raises before the move, so the file stays live (quota-visible) rather than landing in trash pre-expired — the strictly safer failure mode, and it will be logged.

`_safe_original_files(path)` (lines 181-191) globs `<parent>/originals/<path.stem>.*`. `path` comes from the display URL, so an "originals sibling with the display file missing" just means an `originals/<stem>.<ext>` file exists on disk while `<stem>.webp` does not. `path.is_file()` will be False, so the main-file branch is skipped and only the originals loop runs.

### 1. Add module logger (top of file)

Add `import logging` to the stdlib import block (alphabetically, after `import hashlib` / with the other imports, before/around `import os`), and add a module-level logger near the other module constants (e.g. just after the imports, before `MEDIA_URL_PREFIX`):

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

### 2. Rewrite `trash_media` (lines 371-395)

Recommended shape — a tiny local helper that stamps-then-moves with per-file isolation and logging, so a failure moving the display file no longer aborts the originals, and one bad original doesn't strand the rest. ```python
def _stamp_and_trash(src: Path, dest_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Stamp *src*'s mtime to now, then move it into *dest_dir*.

    The mtime is stamped on the source *before* the move so it survives
    both shutil.move paths (same-fs os.rename preserves it; cross-fs
    copy2 copies it), giving the trashed file a fresh retention clock.
    Best-effort: logs and swallows any failure so a delete can't break.
    """
    try:
        os.utime(src, None)
        shutil.move(str(src), str(dest_dir / src.name))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("Failed to trash media file %s", src.name, exc_info=True)


def trash_media(value: str | None) -> None:

    for orig in originals:

- `_safe_original_files(path)` is computed **before** any move (unchanged ordering), since moving the display file must not affect the originals lookup. (In practice originals live in a sibling `originals/` dir keyed on stem, so ordering is not strictly load-bearing, but keeping the pre-computation preserves current behavior.)

    Best-effort: logs and swallows any failure so a delete can't break.

        os.utime(src, None)

    return path


def _trash_originals_dir(tree_dir: Path) -> Path:
    path = (_trash_dir(tree_dir) / "originals").resolve()
    path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    return path


def _stamp_and_trash(src: Path, dest_dir_fn) -> None:
    """Stamp *src*'s mtime to now, then move it into ``dest_dir_fn()``.

    The mtime is stamped on the source *before* the move so it survives
    either path ``shutil.move`` can take: a same-filesystem ``os.rename``
    carries the source mtime through verbatim, and a cross-filesystem
    ``copy2`` fallback copies it from the source. Stamping only the
    destination (after the move) leaves a window where a stale, already-
    expired mtime sits in trash and can be purged before it's corrected.
    Best-effort and per-file: logs and swallows any failure so one bad file
    can't strand its siblings or break the caller's delete request.
    """
    try:
        dest_dir = dest_dir_fn()
        os.utime(src, None)
        shutil.move(str(src), str(dest_dir / src.name))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("Failed to trash media file %s", src.name, exc_info=True)


def trash_media(value: str | None) -> None:
    """Move the on-disk file backing a media URL into the tree's trash.

    Retention counterpart to ``delete_media``: instead of unlinking, the file
    (and any ``originals/`` sibling) is moved into ``<tree_dir>/.trash/`` with
    its mtime stamped to the move time, so ``purge_expired_media_trash`` can
    later reclaim it once ``MEDIA_TRASH_TTL_SECONDS`` has elapsed. No-op for
    non-media URLs or missing files; never raises, so a failed move can't
    break a delete request.
    """
    path = _safe_media_path(value)
    if path is None:
        return
    originals = _safe_original_files(path)
    if path.is_file():
        _stamp_and_trash(path, lambda: _trash_dir(path.parent))
    for orig in originals:
        _stamp_and_trash(orig, lambda: _trash_originals_dir(path.parent))

"""Tests for per-tree storage usage calculation and quota enforcement."""

import base64

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from app.services.storage import _tree_media_dir, delete_tree_media
from app.services.storage_usage import (
    QuotaExceeded,
    _media_bytes,
    _tree_model_bytes,
    check_full_usage_quota,
    check_media_quota,
    check_tree_quota,
    compute_owner_usage,
    compute_usage,
    media_warning,
    owner_quotas,
)
from tests.conftest import API, add_member, auth, make_tree, make_user

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _write_fake_media(tree_id: str, filename: str, content: bytes) -> str:
    """Write a fake media file and return its path string."""
    path = _tree_media_dir(tree_id) / filename
    path.write_bytes(content)
    return str(path)


def _make_tiny_png_data_url() -> str:
    """Return a minimal 1×1 PNG as a data URL."""
    # 1×1 red PNG (binary-safe minimal PNG)
    png_bytes = (
        b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
        b"\x00\x00\x00\rIHDR\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x01\x08\x02"
        b"\x00\x00\x00\x90wS\xde\x00\x00\x00\x0cIDATx\x9cc\xf8\x0f\x00"
        b"\x00\x01\x01\x00\x05\x18\xd8N\x00\x00\x00\x00IEND\xaeB`\x82"
    )
    b64 = base64.b64encode(png_bytes).decode()
    return f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _media_bytes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_media_bytes_missing_dir():
    """media_bytes returns 0 when the tree directory doesn't exist."""
    assert _media_bytes("nonexistent-tree-id-xyz") == 0


def test_media_bytes_sums_files(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """media_bytes sums file sizes under the tree directory."""
    # media_root is a computed property (DATA_PATH/media) — patch DATA_PATH.
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "DATA_PATH", tmp_path)
    tree_id = "test-tree-001"
    _write_fake_media(tree_id, "a.webp", b"hello")
    _write_fake_media(tree_id, "b.webp", b"world!")
    assert _media_bytes(tree_id) == 11  # 5 + 6


def test_media_bytes_zero_after_delete(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """media_bytes returns 0 after delete_tree_media removes the directory."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "DATA_PATH", tmp_path)
    tree_id = "test-tree-002"
    _write_fake_media(tree_id, "photo.webp", b"data")
    assert _media_bytes(tree_id) > 0
    delete_tree_media(tree_id)
    assert _media_bytes(tree_id) == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _tree_model_bytes / compute_usage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_tree_bytes_grows_with_member(db: Session):
    owner = make_user(db, "storage-owner")
    tree = make_tree(db, owner, "StorageTree")

    before = _tree_model_bytes(db, tree.id)
    add_member(db, tree, "m1", first_name="Alice", last_name="Smith")
    after = _tree_model_bytes(db, tree.id)
    assert after > before
